questions.q: Per this lesson, what distinguishes a 'data product' from a plain raw table?
options: It meets characteristics like discoverable, addressable, trustworthy, self-describing, interoperable, and secure — it has real consumers it's built for
It is always stored in exactly one specific database technology
It must be owned by the central IT department
It has no schema of any kind
questions.explain: The lesson lists six characteristics a data product has to meet, which a plain raw table doesn't automatically satisfy.

questions.q: What does 'self-describing' mean for a data product, per this lesson?
options: Its schema, meaning, and classification are documented alongside it, not kept in someone's head or a stale separate wiki
It automatically writes its own source code
It requires no catalog entry at all
It cannot be accessed by any other team
questions.explain: Self-describing means the documentation travels with the product itself, rather than living separately and going stale.

questions.q: Where does this lesson say governance actually attaches to a data product?
options: At the output port, via a data contract specifying schema, quality, classification, and ownership
Inside the domain's internal implementation details, which must be fully exposed
Only in a separate legal contract unrelated to the architecture
Governance never attaches to a data product in any way
questions.explain: The lesson states governance attaches at the output port through a data contract, without needing to reach into the internal build.

questions.q: Per this lesson, is 'data as a product' useful only within a full data-mesh adoption?
options: No — centralized and federated architectures can also adopt data products as the unit of governance
Yes, it is meaningless outside data mesh
Yes, it requires abandoning any other operating model entirely
No, it can only be used by decentralized architectures
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly generalizes the data-product idea beyond mesh, noting centralized hubs and federated shared schemas can both require it.

questions.q: What is a 'data contract,' per this lesson?
options: The schema, quality guarantee, classification, and ownership information that travels with a data product's output port
A legally binding financial agreement between two companies
A password-sharing policy document
An employment agreement for data engineers
questions.explain: The lesson defines a data contract as the governance metadata traveling with the output port, not a financial or employment document.
